Bounded-concurrency precompressed-sibling writer.
Sourcesrc/shared\scripts\build\compress-queue.mjs
UX surfaceBoot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

BROTLI_OPTS

Highest static quality — matches every historical sibling writer.

GZIP_OPTS

Maximum gzip effort — matches vite-plugin-compression2's level.

DRAIN_CONCURRENCY

Drain worker count — ~2× the libuv pool keeps zlib busy without the EMFILE handle exhaustion an unbounded ~19k-task fan-out trips on Windows (each task opens two sibling-write handles at once).

pending

Queued compression tasks — { file, buf } pairs. Buffers are retained until their turn arrives: holding ~19k page buffers (~600MB worst case) is deliberate — re-reading each file would double I/O and invalidate AV-scan residency between write and compress.

writeFileReplace

Writes buf to file, falling back to temp-write + rename when the direct write is refused. On Windows an existing file carrying the NTFS Compressed attribute rejects open-for-truncate (O_TRUNC surfaces as UNKNOWN and never clears); replacing the file through a sibling temp name sidesteps the truncate entirely — and atomic-replaces, so a reader never sees a half-written document.

  • @param {string} file target path
  • @param {Buffer} buf payload

writeFileReplaceAsync

Async sibling of writeFileReplace for the drain workers.

queueCompressedWrite

Writes contents to file synchronously, then queues async brotli-11 + gzip-9 siblings. The sync write keeps every caller's existing "file exists right after the call" assumption; only the compressed siblings defer to the pool.

  • @param {string} file absolute output path
  • @param {string | Buffer} contents document body

runTask

Compresses one queued task — brotli + gzip run concurrently per file (two threadpool slots) and each sibling write retries through withFsRetryAsync so a transient Windows share lock can't fail a multi-thousand-file drain.

  • @param {{file: string, buf: Buffer}} task queued work item
  • @returns {Promise} resolves once both siblings are on disk

drainCompressedWrites

Drains the queue with bounded worker concurrency. The libuv threadpool (sized via UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE at process start) limits zlib work, but each task also opens file handles for the two sibling writes — with ~19k queued tasks, unbounded fan-out opens handles faster than they close and trips EMFILE on Windows. A fixed worker pool keeps at most DRAIN_CONCURRENCY×2 handles in flight. Tasks queued after this call would be missed, so callers must drain exactly once, after the emit loop.

  • @returns {Promise} count of documents compressed

compressedWritesPending

Pending-task count — exposed for progress logs and tests.
